name: e85
source: Derived, not independently sourced: an 85% v/v anhydrous-ethanol / 15% v/v gasoline blend (v = 0.85), computed from this project's own data/fuels/gasoline.json (LHV 44.0 MJ/kg, AFR_s 14.5, density 747.5 kg/m^3) and data/fuels/ethanol.json (LHV 26.8 MJ/kg, AFR_s 9.0, density 794.0 kg/m^3; both ultimately Heywood 1988 Table 9.7) via ideal volume-additive mixing: rho = v*rho_e + (1-v)*rho_g = 787.025 kg/m^3; mass fraction w_e = v*rho_e/rho = 0.857533; LHV = w_e*LHV_e + (1-w_e)*LHV_g = 29,250,430 J/kg (mass-additive, heat of mixing neglected); AFR_s = w_e*AFR_e + (1-w_e)*AFR_g = 9.783568 (exact - stoichiometric air per kg of fuel is mass-additive regardless of mixing). Assumptions: ideal mixing (the small negative excess volume real ethanol-gasoline blends show is neglected), anhydrous ethanol (EN 15376 blending-component composition, not hydrous pump ethanol), and a nominal 85% v/v label composition (EN 15293:2018 defines E85 as NOMINALLY 85% v/v ethanol, with seasonal grades permitted lower - e.g. a winter grade around 70% v/v - so a real pump E85 may differ from this file's exact 85% figure). Range cross-check: 787.025 kg/m^3 is inside EN 15293:2018's 755-800 kg/m^3 density range for E85 at 15 degC.
